title: Introduce response_format adaptor with streaming checkpoints and graceful schema fallback
author: Maya Chen
commits: a1f4c2d: runtime: add response_format adaptor middleware and mapping
b3e5f91: streaming: emit schema checkpoint frames and resume tokens
c9d2a77: openai-compat: map response_format -> response_format_hint header
d4f6e02: api: add strictness query param and per-request enforcement path
e5a8b33: tests: integration tests for streaming schema mismatch recovery
f0c7d44: docs: examples and OpenAPI addition for response_format_hint
description:
Motivation: Customers running schema-validated structured output under streaming have seen brittle failures when the model momentarily emits a malformed fragment or when tool calls interleave with schema frames. This PR introduces a response_format adaptor layer and a streaming checkpoint protocol to make schema enforcement resilient while preserving OpenAI-compatible request parameters.

What this change does: Adds a small middleware (response_format adaptor) that normalizes incoming OpenAI-style response_format/schemas into an internal enforcement hint (response_format_hint). The adaptor maps the OpenAI 'response_format' and 'response_format_options' into three internal enforcement levels: permissive, balanced, and strict. Requests can still pass the legacy parameters; the adaptor emits a response_format_hint header for downstream runtime.

Streaming stability: The runtime now emits explicit schema checkpoint frames (FRAME_SCHEMA_CHECKPOINT) at configurable token watermarks (default every 128 tokens) and attaches a short resume token on each checkpoint. If the incremental validator sees a mismatch mid-stream, the runtime will: 1) inject a structured error frame (SF-104: incremental-schema-mismatch) with a human-readable path and a recommended resume_token, 2) attempt a lightweight soft-repair by rewinding to the last checkpoint and asking the model to re-emit the remainder (when model supports retry), and 3) if repair fails under 'strict' enforcement, surface a final structured failure and trigger the configured fallback (fallback_model or pre-specified offramp).

Tool/function calling safety: When a tool call is initiated during streaming and the response is under strict enforcement, the runtime fences the tool call until the next schema checkpoint is validated to avoid partial tool call inputs. New flags: prevent_partial_tool_calls (runtime config) and toolcall_fence_timeout (per-request). If a toolcall times out while fenced, we emit SF-202 (toolcall-fence-timeout) with metadata including the checkpoint id.

OpenAI compatibility: The param mapper supports legacy OpenAI fields (response_format, response_format_type, response_format_schema) and translates them to response_format_hint. There's also support for the OpenAI 'strict' boolean via mapping to our 'strict' enforcement level. This preserves existing client behavior while enabling opt-in of the durable streaming semantics.

Operational notes: Default behavior is 'balanced' (permissive repair, soft fallback). 'strict' enforcement can be requested per-call via query param or header (x-response-format-strict=true) and will be enforced only when the customer's model is pinned to a compatible variant; otherwise the adaptor returns a 422 with guidance. We added telemetry for checkpoint events (checkpoint_emitted, checkpoint_repaired, checkpoint_fail) to help SRE and customers tune watermarks and timeouts.

Backwards compatibility and rollout: The adaptor is opt-in via a feature flag 'response_format_adaptor' (staged release). We will enable it for a small set of early adopters and then roll to 100% after 2 weeks of monitoring. There are migration docs and an example showing how to send the legacy OpenAI payload and how to adopt the explicit header-based hint.

Testing and QA: Added unit tests for checkpoint manager, integration tests that simulate mid-stream schema corruption and toolcall fencing, and end-to-end examples in the examples/structured_output folder. CI includes a flaky test tolerance for one streaming test which was flapping in the first run and now stabilized after increasing the virtual model response latency in CI.

Related work: This complements ENG-4521 (streaming resiliency) and PM-318 (structured output UX). See migration docs for exact request/response examples.

Rollout/merge: Merged to main via squash after reviewer approvals and a green CI run.

release_notes:
- Add response_format adaptor that maps legacy OpenAI response_format to an internal response_format_hint and three enforcement levels (permissive/balanced/strict).
- Emit streaming schema checkpoints and resume tokens; on incremental schema mismatch the runtime will attempt a soft-repair and provide structured error frames (SF-104).
- Fenced toolcalls during streaming to avoid partial tool inputs; new error SF-202 for fence timeouts.
- OpenAI-compatibility preserved via params mapping and example migration docs.
